assumptions._note: Standalone model (Exide Industries Ltd = the lead-acid business), the basis the street uses for the core (MOFSL, ICICI Securities report standalone numbers). The lithium-ion subsidiary EESL, the HDFC Life stake and other investments are valued separately in the sum of the parts. FY26 base = Screener standalone (revenue Rs17,269 cr, EBITDA Rs1,946 cr, PAT Rs1,111 cr). One segment ('core') so that bull/bear deltas flow through the engine's SOTP scenarios. Core, HDFC Life and EESL values are computed in tools/authoring/EXIDEIND.ctx.js and written here by EXIDEIND.val.js.

segments.name: Lead-acid batteries (standalone Exide)
segments._why: Revenue = sum of five business lines (assumptions.build, checked in EXIDEIND.ctx.js). FY27E +12.9%: Q1FY27 +17.6% (volume double digit in most lines, prices +4-6% YoY), a low Q2 base (Q2FY26 -2% after the GST washout), then a high auto-OEM base in H2 (management, 3-Aug-2026). FY28-29E ~9%: management's medium-term 'high single digit to early double digit' for the core (5-year CAGR 11% +/-1%, Q4FY26 call), replacement demand from the FY26-27 OEM surge (2.5-3 years later), solar and exports recovering; telecom and e-rickshaw keep shifting to lithium.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin (Screener basis): FY26 11.3%, Q1FY27 12.3% (seasonal peak: inverter season; Q2FY26 was 9.5%). FY27E 11.6%: input costs (rupee lead, sulphur up from Rs15 to Rs75/kg, polypropylene) are being passed on in steps; cost-excellence savings. FY28-29E 11.9-12.0%: operating leverage on ~9% growth. Street: MOFSL 11.2%/12.0% FY27-28E, ICICI Securities 11.9%/12.4%.

assumptions._capexWhy: Management keeps ~Rs500 cr a year for the lead-acid business (debottlenecking, automation, brownfield 4W capacity; Q1FY27 call). FY26 capex ~Rs409 cr (MOFSL). Lithium-ion capex sits in EESL, funded by equity infusions (see build.eeslInfusion), not here.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs501 cr; Q1FY27 Rs118 cr (run-rate ~Rs475 cr as older assets reach full depreciation). 7.0% of average gross block gives FY27E ~Rs480 cr. CWIP is held flat by the engine.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Set to zero: the engine's 'treasury' includes the HDFC Life stake (Rs5,140 cr at Mar-26 fair value) and the EESL investment at cost (Rs4,802 cr), which earn no interest. Treasury income is built on liquid funds only, in otherIncome.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built (EXIDEIND.ctx.js checks it): 7% on average liquid funds (cash Rs165 cr + liquid mutual funds Rs254 cr at Mar-26; FY26 treasury income Rs32 cr: mutual-fund gains Rs30.6 cr + interest Rs1.2 cr) after funding EESL infusions, + dividends on investments Rs21-23 cr (HDFC Life, Faering, LIC Housing: Rs18.5 cr in FY26; subsidiaries Rs2.0 cr) + guarantee commission from EESL Rs6 cr (FY26 Rs5.6 cr) + foreign-exchange gains Rs10 cr (FY26 Rs27.9 cr, FY25 Rs9.5 cr; not forecast at the FY26 level) + other Rs7 cr. FY26 (Screener) Rs82 cr; TTM to Jun-2026 Rs79 cr; Q1FY27 Rs14 cr as cash went to EESL.
assumptions._interestWhy: Standalone is debt-free; FY26 finance cost Rs34.9 cr of which lease interest Rs32.9 cr (AR FY26 note 30). Q1FY27 Rs8 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: New regime (25.17%) plus small disallowances: FY26 effective 25.5%, Q1FY27 25.0%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Rs2 per share for FY24-26 (FY26 dividend Rs170 cr proposed, AR FY26 note 16): 15% of FY26 EPS. Cash is being kept for the lithium-ion project.

build._why: Auto (OEM + replacement, domestic): OEM +25% for three quarters on the GST cut, 4W replacement volume +10% in Q1FY27; H2 base high. Home UPS/inverter (Rs2,300 cr, 15-25% of revenue by season): a strong summer in Q1FY27. Solar (crossed Rs1,000 cr in FY26; >Rs400 cr in Q1FY27). Exports (Rs915 cr, ~5%; down from ~8%): +20% in Q1FY27 off a low base. Industrial domestic: infrastructure ex-telecom double digit, government tenders soft until H2FY27, telecom (~2-3%) shrinking.
build._eeslInfusionWhy: FY27E: Board-approved Rs1,400 cr (Rs100 cr paid in July; capex plus operating and working-capital needs). FY28-29E: none in the core cash path. EESL losses after the target date are charged once, as a present value in the EESL line of the sum of the parts (PLAYBOOK §7c); Phase 2 (6 to 12 GWh) is not approved and is excluded.

eesl._lossWhy: GAM estimates (no company guidance; brokers do not publish EESL forecasts). FY26 loss Rs248 cr before commercial production (AOC-1); the consolidated-less-standalone gap was Rs56 cr in Q1FY27. From commercial start in FY27 depreciation on ~Rs4,500-5,000 cr of plant (~Rs300 cr a year) and interest on ~Rs1,200 cr of subsidiary borrowings (consolidated less standalone borrowings at Mar-26) arrive before volumes: management guides 25-30% utilisation of 6 GWh in the first year and 85% utilisation with 90% yield as the target. Base: breakeven in FY30E. Bull: FY30E with smaller losses (PLI-style support, Hyundai-Kia line). Bear: losses persist into FY30E, breakeven FY31E.

dcf._betaWhy: Debt-free consumer-and-industrial battery maker with lead-price pass-through: beta 1.0, cost of equity 12.5%.
dcf._tgWhy: Batteries track vehicle parc, power back-up and industrial capex: ~5.5% nominal long-run growth (house range 5-6%), below India's ~10% nominal GDP as telecom and e-rickshaw move to lithium.
dcf._fadeWhy: Growth fades from ~9% to 7%; margin held at 12% (FY17-26 band 10.7-14.0%); capex 3% of sales (FY27-29E ~2.4-2.6% plus periodic capacity steps); depreciation 2.6% of sales.
dcf._netCashWhy: The engine adds 'treasury' at FY27E: liquid funds + the HDFC Life stake at Mar-26 fair value + EESL and other investments at cost. So the DCF is a core DCF plus those investments at book, a cross-check only.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The post-GST auto cycle and the replacement wave it creates lift volumes; solar and exports keep growing in double digits; price increases stick and margin reaches ~12.5%; EESL ramps faster (losses shrink, breakeven FY30E); HDFC Life valued near market.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Auto-OEM growth reverses against the high base, rupee lead and sulphur costs outrun price increases (margin back to ~11%), telecom and e-rickshaw shift to lithium faster; EESL yields and approvals lag (breakeven FY31E) and the market values the plant at half of book; HDFC Life at a 30% discount.

cover.headline: A sound battery franchise carrying a costly lithium bet: fairly priced at ₹412
cover.lead: Exide is India's largest lead-acid battery maker (car and two-wheeler batteries for vehicle makers and the replacement market, inverter, solar and industrial batteries), one half of a duopoly with Amara Raja. Q1FY27 was strong: standalone revenue +17.6%, EBITDA margin 12.4%, profit +27%. Around this core sit an 8.70 cr-share stake in HDFC Life and a ₹4,902 cr lithium-ion cell plant (EESL) that is only now shipping samples. The street values Exide **in parts**, and so do we: the core at **15.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹19.4 (₹301)** + HDFC Life at market less 20% (₹43) + EESL at book less the present value of losses to breakeven (₹52) + other investments (₹6) = **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD.** Cross-checks: P/E on all standalone EPS ₹372, DCF ₹434. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The core is doing well, and the cycle helps
arguments.p: Auto-OEM sales grew ~25% for three quarters after the September-2025 GST cut, and those batteries come back as replacement demand in 2.5-3 years. Q1FY27 volumes rose double digits in most lines (4W replacement +10%, 4W OEM +21%, 2W OEM +20%) and prices +4-6%. We model revenue +{{F.salesGrowth.0|pct0}} / +{{F.salesGrowth.1|pct0}} / +{{F.salesGrowth.2|pct0}} and EBITDA margin {{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} → {{F.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}}.

arguments.h: But margins are a decade lower and lithium is eating the edges
arguments.p: The margin was 13-15% in FY16-21 and 10.8-11.7% since; lead is bought at import parity, so a weak rupee hurts, and sulphur and plastics rose sharply in FY26. Telecom and e-rickshaw batteries are moving to lithium (exports and telecom shrank to ~5% and ~3% of revenue in FY26). This is a duopoly with steady volumes, not a business with pricing power.

arguments.h: The lithium plant is the swing factor, and it is still a cost
arguments.p: EESL has ₹4,902 cr of Exide's equity, lost ₹248 cr in FY26 and needs ₹1,400 cr more in FY27. It has Chinese technology (SVOLT), imported materials, no PLI subsidy and 25-30% utilisation guided for year one. We value it at book less ₹337 cr of losses still to come (₹52 a share), below the street's ₹70-82 at book or invested capital.

arguments.h: Valuation: the price already pays for the parts
arguments.p: At ₹413 the stock trades at 22.7x our FY28E standalone EPS. Take out the investments (~₹91 a share) and the core trades at 16.6x Sep-28E EPS, against a 17.0x median since the Exide Life sale; auto-component stocks sat 7.8% below their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026. The post-Q1 street median target is ₹501; it assumes higher multiples (16-18x core) and the plant at full book.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): the first quarter against a weak base (Q2FY26 revenue −2%), and whether price increases keep pace with rupee lead and sulphur costs.
Formal start of commercial production at the Bengaluru cell plant and the first cell revenue (guided "during FY27"); customer approvals at the three 2W OEMs that hold ~80% of the EV market.
EESL funding: the Board reviews the ₹1,400 cr FY27 plan; any Phase-2 (6 to 12 GWh) approval or a PLI application under the re-opened 10 GWh tranche.
China's export rules on battery materials (approvals from November) and the end of its export VAT rebate on cells (from 1-Jan-2027), which raises the landed cost of imported cells.
HDFC Life share price: each ₹50 moves our value by ~₹4 a share; any sale of the stake to fund lithium.

sections.title: India's battery for everything: cars, inverters, railways and submarines, sold through 120,000 outlets

blocks.p: Exide Industries (Kolkata, founded 1947, listed 1979) makes lead-acid batteries from 2.5 Ah to 20,200 Ah in 11 plants, buys most of its lead from three recycling plants of its subsidiary Chloride Metals, and sells through 120,000+ touchpoints. About half of revenue is automotive (OEM and replacement) and half non-auto (inverters, solar, industrial); ~65-70% goes through the trade (B2C) channel. It reports one segment. The standalone company is the lead-acid business; two subsidiaries matter: **Exide Energy Solutions (EESL)**, a lithium-ion cell and pack maker building a 12 GWh plant in Bengaluru (6 GWh in phase 1), and **Chloride Metals**, the lead recycler (₹6,036 cr revenue, a ₹14 cr loss in FY26). It also holds **8.70 cr HDFC Life shares** (~4%), received when it sold Exide Life Insurance in 2022.

sections.title: Seventy-nine years of batteries, one big sale (Exide Life) and one big bet (lithium-ion cells)

blocks.p: Exide's promoter is Chloride Eastern Ltd (UK), its holding company by de facto control, with 45.99%. Until 2021 it was a lead-acid maker with a life-insurance subsidiary (Exide Life). Two decisions in 2021-22 reshaped it. It sold Exide Life to HDFC Life (completed 1-Jan-2022) for ₹726 cr of cash and 8.70 cr HDFC Life shares then worth ₹5,653 cr, and it set up EESL (incorporated 24-Mar-2022) to make lithium-ion cells. In effect, the insurance money has been recycled into the cell plant: ₹4,902 cr of equity by Jul-2026, roughly what the HDFC Life shares were worth at receipt.

sections.title: A two-player lead-acid market enjoying a post-GST car boom while lithium takes the edges

blocks.p: Indian lead-acid batteries are a duopoly in the organised market: Exide and Amara Raja (ARE&M) lead auto OEM and replacement; Exide leads industrial (railways, traction, power, submarine, UPS) except telecom. The replacement channel (B2C) is ~65-70% of Exide's business (AR FY26). Auto OEM grew ~25% YoY for three straight quarters after the GST cut (28% to 18% on batteries and vehicles, effective 22-Sep-2025); replacement demand follows OEM fitments 2.5-3 years later (Q1FY27 call). Home inverters/UPS ~15-25% of revenue by season; solar crossed ₹1,000 cr in FY26 (PM Surya Ghar rooftop scheme).

bullets: **The tailwind reaches Exide's volumes.** It is the largest OEM supplier, so the post-GST production jump shows up at once, and the bigger car parc feeds replacement demand later.

**It reaches margins only partly.** Lead is priced at import parity and the rupee is weak; sulphur rose about five-fold in FY26. sections.title: Revenue up 2.5 times in ten years, but margins fell from 14-15% to 11%: a volume business that lost its premium

blocks.p: Standalone revenue (the lead-acid business) was ₹6,795 cr in FY16 and ₹17,269 cr in FY26: 9.8% a year, and 11.5% a year since FY21. Growth came from volumes and from passing on lead and other input costs; FY26 grew only 4% after a lost quarter around the September-2025 GST change. The EBITDA margin is the weak spot: 13.3-15.0% in FY16-21, then 10.8-11.7% since FY22 as input costs rose faster than prices, competition from Amara Raja stayed tight and telecom and e-rickshaw batteries moved to lithium. Reported profit is muddled by one item: FY22 includes the ₹4,694 cr pre-tax gain on selling Exide Life to HDFC Life. Before it, EPS rose from ₹8.9 (FY21) to ₹13.1 (FY26), 8% a year.

bullets: **Cash conversion is good.** Cash from operations was ₹2,231 cr in FY26 (201% of profit, 115% of EBITDA) as payables rose; ₹1,298 cr in FY25 (121% of profit).
**One large one-off, clearly labelled.** FY22 profit includes the ₹4,694 cr pre-tax Exide Life gain; FY26 a ₹9 cr labour-code charge. We value on EPS before both.

**Other income is small and mostly real.** FY26 ₹93 cr (company): mutual-fund gains ₹30.6 cr, dividends ₹20.5 cr, foreign-exchange gains ₹27.9 cr, guarantee commission from EESL ₹5.6 cr, other ₹8.4 cr. sections.title: The street after Q1: four Buys, one Neutral, one Sell; median target ₹501

blocks.p: Six houses updated after the Q1FY27 results (3/4-Aug-2026): Buy from ICICI Securities (₹520), J.P. Morgan (₹514), Citi (₹510) and Nomura (₹492), Neutral from Motilal Oswal (₹419) and Sell from Kotak (₹325). The median target is ₹501, +21% vs the 30-Sep-2026 close of ₹413; the stock had traded at ~₹450 in early August. The two houses that publish their method both use a **sum of the parts**: the core on FY28E standalone EPS (16x MOFSL, 18x ICICI), the lithium-ion plant at book or invested capital (₹82 and ₹70 a share) and the HDFC Life stake separately (₹45; ICICI ₹90 a share including other subsidiaries). Before Q1, Nuvama had cut to Reduce (₹300) on cost pressure. The bulls focus on the OEM-led cycle and the cell plant starting up; the bears on returns from lithium.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a good battery business, a costly cell bet, and a price that already adds them up; HOLD

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's leading lead-acid battery franchise (half of a duopoly, the biggest brand and distribution network, captive lead recycling), debt-free and cash-generative, in a good cycle (post-GST auto boom, inverters, solar, a replacement wave to come). Attached to it: an HDFC Life stake worth ~₹53 a share at market, and a lithium-ion cell plant that has absorbed ₹4,902 cr and is only now shipping samples. Margins are ordinary (~11-12%) and returns on equity are ~8% because of the investments.

**What you are paying:** ₹413 is 26.0x our FY27E and 22.7x FY28E standalone EPS. Net of the investments, the core trades at 16.6x Sep-28E EPS vs a 17.0x median since 2022, while auto-component stocks were 7.8% below their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026. Our sum of the parts gives {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): HOLD. The street's higher targets (median ₹501) need a 16-18x core and the plant at full book; we do not see why the core should get more than its own history, or the plant more than what has been put in, before it has sold a cell.

segments.name: Lead-acid batteries (standalone Exide)
segments._why: Revenue = sum of five business lines (assumptions.build, checked in EXIDEIND.ctx.js). FY27E +12.9%: Q1FY27 +17.6% (volume double digit in most lines, prices +4-6% YoY), a low Q2 base (Q2FY26 -2% after the GST washout), then a high auto-OEM base in H2 (management, 3-Aug-2026). FY28-29E ~9%: management's medium-term 'high single digit to early double digit' for the core (5-year CAGR 11% +/-1%, Q4FY26 call), replacement demand from the FY26-27 OEM surge (2.5-3 years later), solar and exports recovering; telecom and e-rickshaw keep shifting to lithium.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin (Screener basis): FY26 11.3%, Q1FY27 12.3% (seasonal peak: inverter season; Q2FY26 was 9.5%). FY27E 11.6%: input costs (rupee lead, sulphur up from Rs15 to Rs75/kg, polypropylene) are being passed on in steps; cost-excellence savings. FY28-29E 11.9-12.0%: operating leverage on ~9% growth. Street: MOFSL 11.2%/12.0% FY27-28E, ICICI Securities 11.9%/12.4%.

assumptions._capexWhy: Management keeps ~Rs500 cr a year for the lead-acid business (debottlenecking, automation, brownfield 4W capacity; Q1FY27 call). FY26 capex ~Rs409 cr (MOFSL). Lithium-ion capex sits in EESL, funded by equity infusions (see build.eeslInfusion), not here.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs501 cr; Q1FY27 Rs118 cr (run-rate ~Rs475 cr as older assets reach full depreciation). 7.0% of average gross block gives FY27E ~Rs480 cr. CWIP is held flat by the engine.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Set to zero: the engine's 'treasury' includes the HDFC Life stake (Rs5,140 cr at Mar-26 fair value) and the EESL investment at cost (Rs4,802 cr), which earn no interest. Treasury income is built on liquid funds only, in otherIncome.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built (EXIDEIND.ctx.js checks it): 7% on average liquid funds (cash Rs165 cr + liquid mutual funds Rs254 cr at Mar-26; FY26 treasury income Rs32 cr: mutual-fund gains Rs30.6 cr + interest Rs1.2 cr) after funding EESL infusions, + dividends on investments Rs21-23 cr (HDFC Life, Faering, LIC Housing: Rs18.5 cr in FY26; subsidiaries Rs2.0 cr) + guarantee commission from EESL Rs6 cr (FY26 Rs5.6 cr) + foreign-exchange gains Rs10 cr (FY26 Rs27.9 cr, FY25 Rs9.5 cr; not forecast at the FY26 level) + other Rs7 cr. FY26 (Screener) Rs82 cr; TTM to Jun-2026 Rs79 cr; Q1FY27 Rs14 cr as cash went to EESL.
assumptions._interestWhy: Standalone is debt-free; FY26 finance cost Rs34.9 cr of which lease interest Rs32.9 cr (AR FY26 note 30). Q1FY27 Rs8 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: New regime (25.17%) plus small disallowances: FY26 effective 25.5%, Q1FY27 25.0%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Rs2 per share for FY24-26 (FY26 dividend Rs170 cr proposed, AR FY26 note 16): 15% of FY26 EPS. Cash is being kept for the lithium-ion project.

build._why: Auto (OEM + replacement, domestic): OEM +25% for three quarters on the GST cut, 4W replacement volume +10% in Q1FY27; H2 base high. Home UPS/inverter (Rs2,300 cr, 15-25% of revenue by season): a strong summer in Q1FY27. Solar (crossed Rs1,000 cr in FY26; >Rs400 cr in Q1FY27). Exports (Rs915 cr, ~5%; down from ~8%): +20% in Q1FY27 off a low base. Industrial domestic: infrastructure ex-telecom double digit, government tenders soft until H2FY27, telecom (~2-3%) shrinking.
build._eeslInfusionWhy: FY27E: Board-approved Rs1,400 cr (Rs100 cr paid in July; capex plus operating and working-capital needs). FY28-29E: none in the core cash path. EESL losses after the target date are charged once, as a present value in the EESL line of the sum of the parts (PLAYBOOK §7c); Phase 2 (6 to 12 GWh) is not approved and is excluded.

eesl._lossWhy: GAM estimates (no company guidance; brokers do not publish EESL forecasts). FY26 loss Rs248 cr before commercial production (AOC-1); the consolidated-less-standalone gap was Rs56 cr in Q1FY27. From commercial start in FY27 depreciation on ~Rs4,500-5,000 cr of plant (~Rs300 cr a year) and interest on ~Rs1,200 cr of subsidiary borrowings (consolidated less standalone borrowings at Mar-26) arrive before volumes: management guides 25-30% utilisation of 6 GWh in the first year and 85% utilisation with 90% yield as the target. Base: breakeven in FY30E. Bull: FY30E with smaller losses (PLI-style support, Hyundai-Kia line). Bear: losses persist into FY30E, breakeven FY31E.

dcf._betaWhy: Debt-free consumer-and-industrial battery maker with lead-price pass-through: beta 1.0, cost of equity 12.5%.
dcf._tgWhy: Batteries track vehicle parc, power back-up and industrial capex: ~5.5% nominal long-run growth (house range 5-6%), below India's ~10% nominal GDP as telecom and e-rickshaw move to lithium.
dcf._fadeWhy: Growth fades from ~9% to 7%; margin held at 12% (FY17-26 band 10.7-14.0%); capex 3% of sales (FY27-29E ~2.4-2.6% plus periodic capacity steps); depreciation 2.6% of sales.
dcf._netCashWhy: The engine adds 'treasury' at FY27E: liquid funds + the HDFC Life stake at Mar-26 fair value + EESL and other investments at cost. So the DCF is a core DCF plus those investments at book, a cross-check only.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The post-GST auto cycle and the replacement wave it creates lift volumes; solar and exports keep growing in double digits; price increases stick and margin reaches ~12.5%; EESL ramps faster (losses shrink, breakeven FY30E); HDFC Life valued near market.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Auto-OEM growth reverses against the high base, rupee lead and sulphur costs outrun price increases (margin back to ~11%), telecom and e-rickshaw shift to lithium faster; EESL yields and approvals lag (breakeven FY31E) and the market values the plant at half of book; HDFC Life at a 30% discount.
